reader.requirement: A START without the KEY phrase uses the relation EQUAL: it succeeds only on a record whose prime key equals the record key item, and is invalid key (23) otherwise.

edition-consulted.switches: COBOL-85-only mandatory INVALID KEY on START (COBOL6826); not the rule's behaviour

reader.edition-search: grep 'Edition|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior' over src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO/*.cs: the only indexed-connector edition reads are IndexedConnector#SelectSequentialRecord (IndexedReadPreviousAfterOpenAtEnd, READ PREVIOUS only) and #ReadRandom (IndexedDuplicateKeyStatusSequentialOnly, random READ '02' only); neither is on this rule's path. KeyedIoEmitter has no edition read. BindStart maps a missing KEY phrase to op "==" with no edition test.
reader.witnesses-cover: all of the rule's range at this edition (the witness separates EQUAL from >= with a value between two records)

probes.printed: AB02 -> 00; AB99 (between AB02 and CD03) -> 23; LOW-VALUES -> 23; EF04 (the last key) -> 00
COBOL5506 unexpected 'R-ALT' ... expected EQUAL, GREATER ... (KEY without an operator is refused)
probes.expected: the 1985 format requires the operator when KEY is written

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.4.7.4 GR2  (║4.7.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: KeyedIoBinder.BindStart sets op to "==" when startKeyPhrase is absent, and Start maps it to SeekRelation.Equal with a prefix compare. The probes reproduce the witness's distinction.

refuter.evidence: The reader's probe showed a value between two records gives 23 under the implied EQUAL, and this edition's format has no other default form. My q6 probe confirmed that the explicit = and EQUAL spellings select an equal key and that a missing key gives 23. Nothing at --std 85 changes the operator BindStart implies. cite.py: OK §1985:IX.4.7.4 GR2 the text is in GR2.
